body.text: Thu, 3 Sept, 8:10 pm, Final score, Dockers 40, Hawks 72
AFL grand final 2026 live: Dockers lose Alex Pearce to injury against Lions at MCG
The Dockers are dealt a blow in the grand final against the Lions, with inspirational captain Alex Pearce forced from the field with injury.

The Lions are at full-strength after Lachie Neale's dramatic appeal board win on Thursday night, but will the Dockers be able to use Wharfie Time to get them home in their first grand final since 2013?
Follow the live blog below, keep up to date with all the latest stats in our ScoreCentre, and tune in to our live radio coverage.

Live updates
Recap
Here's all the headlines so far:
• Kylie Minogue put in one of the most iconic pre-game shows in grand final history
• Charlie Cameron drew first blood for the Lions after early misses from both teams
• Fremantle's Josh Treacy answered immediately back to get the Dockers on the board
• Treacy was then controversially denied a mark on the quarter time siren with the kick deemed not 15m
• Brisbane's Conor McKenna kicked a stunning dribbling goal to kick off the second half
• Dockers skipper Alex Pearce collapsed to the ground with an apparent achilles injury in sad scenes

Oscar Allen gets another for Brisbane!
The Lions are on the charge again!
They go through the corridor, Will Ashcroft provides the chip to Oscar Allen, and the big man marks near teh 50m arc.
His kick wobbles a bit, but it comes round, and through!
It's back to under a goal the difference!
Kai Lohmann kicks a vital goal for Brisbane!
The Lions just surged it forward with Cam Rayner getting it free to Conor McKenna.
The Irishman didn't go for goal, but he chipped to a target and then a handball over the top to Kai Lohmann, who took it in the goalsquare and hoofed it into the second tier!
Dudley kicks another and Freo kick clear!
Fremantle has the advantage, but they haven't been able to take their chances - until now!
They sent it forward, and Isaiah Dudley went to take it, but Conor McKenna came in to stop him but slid.
Dudley scrambled, took a couple of steps and curled it home!
That's a huge moment for Freo - they lead by 15 points, that's the biggest margin of the day.
Big problems for Dockers as skipper Alex Pearce is injured
This is no good for Fremantle.
The Lions were breaking downfield, and Freo skipper Alex Pearce was chasing over to cover the bouncing ball, when suddenly he stumbled and went down
He can't put any weight ion his right leg - it might be a calf or an Achilles, but whatever it is, it's not good.
He's sitting on the bench, and it's fair to say it looks like the end of his game.
Amiss gets the early goal for Fremantle
The Dockers tall timber is doing the job here!
They go forward and hit their target - this time it's Jye Amiss, 15m out to the left of goal.
He kicks it! The Dockers lead by seven points early doors.
Josh Treacy misses an early chance
The Dockers start strongly, and they get the ball down to Josh Treacy, who marks and prompts another big roar from the purple-dressed contingent in the crowd.
His kick looks like it's through - but it's faded wide!
That's a miss. Dockers need to take these chances and kick clear.
Fair crowds in Freo
The streets are busy in Fremantle right now...
Can the Dockers go on with it?

The concern going into this game was that only three of the Dockers (Luke Jackson, Shai Bolton and Mason Cox) had grand final experience, whereas only two or three of the Lions have not played in a decider.
But to be fair to men from Fremantle, they haven't played like this was their first crack at the big one.
They have held their own and put pressure on the Lions. Particularly those clearances and centre clearances, with Caleb Serong (eight clearances) and Andrew Brayshaw (four) leading the pack.

The question now is, if it stays this close, will Brisbane's institutional memory see them home in a fourth straight grand final, or will the Dockers find that extra burst of energy to get the job done?
Can't wait to find out.
Time for the grand final sprint - it's Jed Walter again!
Here we go for the grand final sprint, and last year's winner Jed Walter from Gold Coast is in there again.
They're off, and Tassie Devils young gun Brandon Leary showed blazing pace early on the outside, he was leading at halfway.
But then Walter turned on the afterburners, and surged clear - he had his arms in the air with 25 to go, and he won easily to go back-to-back!
Well done Jed.

Kylie's performance was a medley of some of her greatest hits from across the decades of her incredible career.
Here are the tracks she crammed into the show:

• In Your Eyes
• Get Outta My Way
• On a Night like This
• All the Lovers

• Slow

Look, Kylie has A LOT of songs.
I'm keen to hear which other ones you would have like to have seen her perform today.

Dockers edging ahead in the stats department
Fremantle leads the inside 50s 27-25, and the Dockers have turned around the clearances so they lead 21-15.
The big key is the centre breaks, with Fremantle having seven to Brisbane's two in that quarter.
If that continues, that will be a definite problem for the Lions.
A look at Kylie's setup from above
Here's how the show would have looked to some very lucky pigeons who just happened to be flying by at the time:
That giant disco-Kylie-football was enormous.
I have no idea what they plan on doing with it now the show is over, but I think it should go in a museum.
Recapping Kylie's cameos
Let's use this half-time break to look back at that cracking show from Kylie Minogue.
It will go down in history as one of her best shows, but she wasn't the only one the spotlight.
She brought composer and multi-instrumentalist musician William Barton on stage for Confide in Me:
Then GFlip returned after their earlier set for Padam Padam:
Then there were the blokes from The Inspired Unemployed for Loco-Motion:
And there was a cheeky Dom Dolla appearance for the big finish.
Key Event
HT: Fremantle, Brisbane tied at 6.7 (43)
The Dockers have the last chance of the half, but it breaks down and the siren sounds.
How good a half was that? Big hits, great goals, fierce contests, and some great marks. Can't ask for more than that, really.
The Lions were looking a bit dicey halfway through the quarter, but they found their way again and it's fitting that we're level again at the main break.
Do NOT go anywhere. This is shaping as a ripper of a grand final.
This is some game!
This grand final is not slowing down!
A brilliant kick to the wing saw Josh Treacy outpoint Lachie Neale.
The Dockers went down the wing, but made a poor decision and the move broke down.
Then it rebounded, and Karl Worner thumped the daylights out of it from 55. It drifted wide!
Scores are level!
Lachie Neale cops the boos - and misses a goal
Lachie Neale has not been a central figure so far, but he had his chance there.
He marked inside 50, prompting a right SPRAY of boos from the crowd ... and then his kick slewed wide.
Lions lead by a point.
